note: Pass 5 of the identity-collision triage (2026-11-15), continuing from docs/reconcile_2026-11-13/identity_collisions_triaged.json's 376 real_candidates. Prior passes investigated Buncombe (fixed, single-source stale snapshot), Spartanburg+qPayBill (fixed, shared bulk-buyer identifier), McDowell (fixed, PDF column-misalignment), Gaston (genuine disagreement, left unresolved), Henderson (deprioritized, too complex). This pass sampled 15 NEW counties never before investigated, live-verified a representative sample of keys in each against the NC statewide OneMap ArcGIS parcel layer (services.nconemap.gov/.../NC1Map_Parcels/FeatureServer/1) and/or the repo's local parcel_cache sqlite caches, and found ZERO new Buncombe/McDowell-shaped single-source-staleness cases -- every lead that looked superficially fixable (one parcel key, two sources, two addresses) resolved on live verification to one of two confirmed-not-a-bug shapes, or to a genuine unresolvable cross-source disagreement. No board patch was applied this pass because no case met the live-verified 'one side is simply wrong' bar; this is a documented negative result, not a skipped step.

liensnc_bulk_pin_pattern.summary: BY FAR the dominant mechanism behind the real_candidates remaining in this list. counties_generic.liensnc scrapes NC 'lien-agent appointment' filings (src/foreclosure_scraper/liensnc_handoff.py docstring, line ~32-34: 'parcel_id = the cell's PIN'). A lien-agent appointment is filed PER CONSTRUCTION PROJECT/LOAN under NC law, not per individual lot -- the clerk's PIN field cites one anchor/reference parcel for the whole project, while scrape_liensnc._extract_address pulls each individual filing's own lot address. Confirmed live via parcel_cache/GIS in every sampled case where the parcel's GIS owner matched: the shared owner is always a bulk entity -- an HOA/POA (Pinewild Property Owners Assoc, Seven Lakes West Landowners, Captains Landing POA, Figure 8 Beach HOA, Summerhouse on Everett Bay), a home builder/developer (Bill Clark Homes, DFC Montrose LLC, Cumberland Homes, Southern Hills NC LLC, IOM Developers, Front Street-Wallburg, New Covenant Partners VI LLC), or an institution (Charlotte-Mecklenburg Hospital, Wake Forest University, NC Department of Transportation). Each row under one key is a genuinely different real lien filing (distinct case/entry number) against a genuinely different real address within that one project/HOA/institution's footprint. This is NOT a pipeline bug and NOT staleness -- it is how NC lien-agent-appointment filings are structured at the source. Counties confirmed this pass: Mecklenburg (via city_websites.charlotte_open_data, the sibling code-enforcement-complaint shape for large apartment complexes -- same underlying mechanism, one big MULTI FAMILY parcel with many per-building violation cases), Guilford, Cabarrus, Harnett, Moore, Forsyth, part of New Hanover and Rutherford.
liensnc_bulk_pin_pattern.action: Do not chase further as individual 'bugs' -- this generalizes the existing same-street/multi-building-complex false-positive bucket far beyond its original scope. A future triage pass could formally fold any key whose liensnc/charlotte_open_data rows all share one owner into this bucket programmatically (same owner_name across every row under the key, source in {counties_generic.liensnc, city_websites.charlotte_open_data}) without further manual sampling, likely re-classifying a large fraction of the remaining real_candidates as false positives of this shape. Not attempted this pass -- would need the owner match verified in code for every row, not just the samples checked here, and is a bigger change to identity_collisions_triaged.json's bucket counts than this pass's authorized scope (sample + document + patch verified staleness only).

mobile_home_park_lot_lh_pattern.summary: LIVE-VERIFIED this pass via Granville County. counties_nc.nc_its_public_tax's parcel field for mobile-home-park lots carries an 'LH##' lot-account suffix (e.g. '086504627424LH3', '088601480320LH'). Querying the NC statewide OneMap parcel layer for the BASE parcel (suffix stripped) confirms the base land parcel belongs to the PARK OPERATOR, not the mobile-home resident: '086504627424' -> owner BLACKLEY ROBERT, situs WELLONS DR; '086504703664' -> owner DUTCH VILLAGE LLC, situs GATE 1 RD (literally a mobile-home-community name); '088601480320' -> owner MOBILE VILLAGE LLC, situs HOLLY DR. Each LH-suffixed board row is a DIFFERENT real resident's own lot-tax-account (Colcough Danny, Gerardi Mark, Bullock Donald, Hernandez Juan, Manchame Mauricio) correctly citing the park's shared land parcel. This is the SAME underlying shape as the already-accepted 'likely_false_positive_mobile_home' bucket (Dillon county SC) and the SC:dillon qPayBill-vs-dillon_delinquent_tax pairs sampled this pass -- just surfacing via a different, NC-specific scraper (nc_its_public_tax) and a different county (Granville) that weren't in scope when the original 50-key mobile-home bucket was built. One of nc_its_public_tax's two rows per key is often a garbled address fragment (e.g. '086504 043LH34', '086504 043 LH') rather than the resident's real street address -- a genuine extraction quirk in that parser when a mobile-home sub-account has no clean situs in the county's own export, same CLASS of issue as the already-fixed McDowell bug, but NOT the same fix: there is no single 'correct value' to patch toward here, because the garbled row and the clean-address row usually represent two genuinely different resident accounts (confirmed by a real owner mismatch in 1 of the 4 sampled keys), not one stale copy of the same fact.
mobile_home_park_lot_lh_pattern.action: Left alone -- matches an accepted false-positive shape, not independently patchable the way Buncombe/McDowell were. Worth a future note in the triage bucket taxonomy: extend 'likely_false_positive_mobile_home' to also catch nc_its_public_tax parcel IDs ending in a letter+digit lot-account suffix (regex roughly [A-Z]{1,3}\d*$ after the numeric parcel), which would likely reclassify Duplin's and Onslow's nc_its_public_tax collisions here too even though those two specific counties' sampled pairs did not carry an obvious LH-style suffix and were not live-verifiable with the NC1Map_Parcels id-field lookup used here (their raw parcel strings, e.g. '03-651--' vs '03-65-1-', did not resolve on parno/altparno/nparno either as given or with the suffix stripped) -- genuinely unresolved, not confirmed either way.

transylvania_damage_assessment_rural_mul.summary: LIVE-VERIFIED via transylvania_vacant/transylvania_delinquent_tax (matches parcel_cache GIS exactly in every sampled case) vs counties_generic.arcgis_distress.transylvania_damage_assessment (Layer config in arcgis_distress_layers.py line ~381: parcel='pin', situs_parts=('house_number','road_name') -- read directly from the county's own storm-damage-assessment ArcGIS layer per inspected structure, not synthesized). Investor/LLC-owned rural tracts (Little Mountain Properties Of, Graace Properties LLC, Frady Ralph &) show MANY damage-assessment rows at sequential house numbers on roads different from the land parcel's own GIS site address -- consistent with multiple storm-damaged structures (likely mobile homes or small rental units) legitimately sitting on one large rural land PIN, the same rationale already accepted for the Dillon mobile-home bucket.
transylvania_damage_assessment_rural_mul.action: Left alone, confirmed not a bug -- same disposition as mobile_home_park_lot_lh_pattern above.

genuine_disagreements_left_unresolved.detail: liensnc '7171 Carolina Beach Rd' confirmed correct via live parcel_cache; arcgis_distress.new_hanover_demolition_permits '1327 SALIENT PT' does not match. The demolition-permit layer reads NUMBER/STREET/PID directly from the city's own permit record (arcgis_distress_layers.py line ~418-449), not a synthesized address -- a city permit genuinely can carry a different accurate address for a specific demolished structure on a multi-structure parcel, or the city's own PID entry for that permit could be wrong. Gaston-shaped: both sides are independently authoritative, no pipeline staleness bug found, not patched.
Same liensnc-vs-demolition_permits PID-disagreement shape as above; not cached locally for an independent GIS cross-check. Left unresolved.

Per the now-understood liensnc PIN-is-literal-from-the-filing design (see liensnc_bulk_pin_pattern), '297 Sherwood Dr' is more likely a different, separately-filed lien against a different property the same heirs own, correctly citing a PIN the county filing itself used, than a staleness bug -- not patched.

None of the 376 keys were removed from real_candidates or reclassified in identity_collisions_triaged.json this pass -- this file only adds documentation alongside it.
estimate_of_remaining_unresolved.note_on_123: Spread across roughly 70-80 other counties/zips in the real_candidates list, each with 1-3 keys -- the long tail. Given this pass found liensnc's bulk-PIN pattern dominates virtually every multi-row county sampled (13 of 15), a reasonable working assumption for the next pass is that most of the remaining 123 keys are liensnc-or-similar bulk-pattern false positives too, but that is an extrapolation, not independently verified.
